title: FedSkill: Privacy Preserved Interpretable Skill Learning via Imitation

problem.claim: Imitation learning must support trustworthy, interpretable policy learning while incorporating expert demonstrations distributed across privacy-sensitive client data silos.

gap.claim: Existing methods lack intrinsic interpretability, and learning from separate client data silos is difficult when expert demonstrations are scarce and privacy or data sovereignty constraints apply.

contributions.claim: FedSkill is a privacy-preserved interpretable skill learning framework for global policy learning across different data sources while providing explainable interpretations to local users.

The interpretable skill learning model captures varying trajectory patterns and extracts prototypical information as skills that guide policy learning and support explicit reasoning-process explanations.
A skill-learning aggregation mechanism is designed to preserve global information utilization and local interpretability within a federated framework.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe FedSkill as the first attempt to bridge federated learning, interpretable machine learning, and imitation learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three datasets and empirical studies reportedly show that FedSkill outperforms state-of-the-art imitation learning methods and exhibits good interpretability in a federated setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Imitation learning has succeeded in replicating expert skills from demonstrations for decision-making tasks.
Real-world deployment is hindered by inadequate interpretability and the difficulty of learning from privacy-sensitive, distributed client data.
FedSkill combines privacy-preserved federated policy learning with local explainable interpretations and prototypical skill extraction.
Its aggregation mechanism aims to retain global information use while maintaining local interpretability.
The authors report favorable comparative performance and interpretability across three datasets, positioning the framework as a bridge among three learning areas.

source_observation.claim: Extracted prototypical information can provide both implicit guidance for policy learning and explicit explanations of the reasoning process.

interpretation.claim: A shared representation may serve both decision support and interpretability when it captures recurring patterns in expert trajectories.

application.claim: In distributed imitation-learning settings, represent expert behavior with reusable prototypes that can guide local policies and explain decisions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether prototype-based explanations remain reliable for behaviors or client distributions not represented in the demonstrations.

source_observation.claim: The proposed aggregation mechanism is intended to preserve global information utilization and local interpretability under federation.

interpretation.claim: Federated aggregation may need to balance shared learning benefits against the interpretability requirements of individual clients.

application.claim: When designing privacy-sensitive collaborative learning, evaluate aggregation not only for global performance but also for preservation of local explanations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the privacy guarantees, aggregation details, or conditions under which local interpretability is maintained.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not specify the privacy mechanism, threat model, or formal data-sovereignty guarantees.
The abstract does not provide details about the skill model, aggregation mechanism, or interpretability evaluation.
